neighbours.label: ' that' directly after 'care' or 'matter' ("don't care that much", "doesn't matter that …"): 'that' taken as the complement of a (not-)mattering predicate. Not 'that' after say/think verbs, relative 'that' or plain degree 'that'. The - pole takes the embedded wh-word (which/where/when) instead.
fire: My sister really doesn't care that much for seafood.
To the judges it didn't matter that she had started late.
Most voters don't seem to care that the budget is overdue.
In the end it hardly matters that the paint is a shade too dark.
We never used to care that much about the weather.
Does it even matter that nobody read the report?
The kids did not care that the film was in black and white.
For this recipe it won't matter that the butter is cold.
quiet: My sister really believes that seafood is overrated.
The judges announced that she had started late.
Most voters seem to think that the budget is overdue.
The paint that we chose is a shade too dark.
We never used to talk that much about the weather.
Did anybody notice that nobody read the report?
The kids complained that the film was in black and white.
For this recipe make sure that the butter is cold.

notes: Card: ' that' x19, top examples all after care/matter. Probe: care that 0.90, matter that 0.75, mind that 0.26, said that 0.02, relative that 0.02, 'not that tall' 0.01.
